items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I did three albums with Maxine and they were albums devoted to songwriters who were still alive: Burton Lane we did... I was so lucky to get to meet these guys, you know... I met Jule Styne and Burton Lane and to actually meet the songwriters and go to their apartment.

ctx.x: Well it’s about this rich lady up in the penthouse in a high rise in Manhattan right? And she’s singing about how lonely she is and she says, “even the janitor’s wife has got a perfectly good sex life, but here am I all alone on the ninetieth floor.” I mean Porter’s stuff is very risqué and so was Lorenz Hart and a lot of his lyrics. There were alternate lyrics to “Bewitched, Bothered and Bewildered” that are pretty raunchy. But I mean everything now has to be let it all hang out and that stuff, but I like some…
And why did they last so long?
